summary: Underware's site for Kermit, Microsoft's 'writable' font for children with a built-in time axis that draws letters stroke by stroke. Four full-screen views switched by icons in the four corners (▶ Experience, ✎ Write, 📖 Read, 👁 Look): a glyph drawn on with its Bézier points, a tester that replays your text being written, three essays, and a poster gallery. Only the splash and the first essay were captured; Write and Look exist only in the HTML.

instances.look: Dark blue-grey screen with soft diagonal light streaks; one big glyph (a '2', on other loads a 'K' or '&') drawn as a hot-pink outline with Bézier points and handles, captioned 'This is Kermit / And this is the number two (Roman, wght 266) / They say it takes two to tango' above small Underware and Microsoft logos
instances.feel: Calm and wondrous, like watching a pen write in the dark
instances.ux: The outline draws itself stroke by stroke after a ~4s load (storyboard: partial '2' at 4.7s, complete by 7.9s); a hidden '▶write' button and a 0–1000 slider (#splashSlider) replay and scrub the writing; the glyph and its caption are picked at random per visit
instances.learn: Introduce a time-based font by letting the hero glyph write itself as an outline with its points visible: the mechanism is the message

reconstruction.layout: Full screen 1440×900; glyph centred ~520px tall from y≈140; title ~44px centred at y≈670; two italic caption lines below; logos ~80px wide at y≈795; four corner icons ~24px at 24px insets
reconstruction.typography: Title 'This is Kermit' ~44px KermitRoman wght 266, light grey; captions ~13px KermitItalic grey, the second naming the glyph, style and weight in parentheses; glyph outline stroke 2–3px #f06 with ~8px round nodes and handle lines
reconstruction.behaviour: SVG lines and nodes (#splashSVG) revealed in stroke order on load; splashSlider (0–1000) scrubs the write-on, the ▶write button replays it; random glyph per load with a matching witty caption
reconstruction.content: One glyph plus a pun about it ('They say it takes two to tango', 'The name Kermit starts with this')
reconstruction.html: section.screen#screen1 > svg#splashSVG + div#splashText (h1 + h2#splashLine1 + h2#splashLine2) + div#splashInterface (button#splashButton + input#splashSlider) + .logos

instances.look: No bar: four line icons fixed in the four corners of every screen, ▶ (Experience, pink or green) top-left, a pen (Write) top-right, an open book (Read) bottom-left, an eye (Look) bottom-right; never cut as its own block
instances.ux: Each corner switches the full-screen view (Experience / Write / Read / Look); the Read view adds a centre-left button that opens an index of the three essays
instances.learn: Four views, four corners: a navigation a child can learn without reading

reconstruction.layout: Fixed icons ~24×24px at 24px from each viewport corner; views are full-screen sections faded in and out (opacity) rather than scrolled
reconstruction.behaviour: Click a corner → the matching section.screen gets opacity 1; the play icon recolours per view
reconstruction.content: Section names live only in the HTML descriptions: '1 Experience: this is Kermit', '2. Write: font tester', '3. Read: 3 stories about Kermit', '4. Look: pictures and details'
reconstruction.assets: Four line icons (play, pen, book, eye)
reconstruction.html: nav > #topBar + button.center-left.nav-button2 (essay index) + corner buttons; section.screen[description]

instances.variantDefinition: Editable samples in a font with a time (write-on) axis: a play button draws the typed text stroke by stroke and a timeline slider scrubs the writing progress, instead of size or style controls.
instances.look: Not captured (the Write screen came out black). From the HTML: six stacked editable samples in Kermit Roman and Italic at weights 100–800 ('I can write.', 'I am Kermit.', 'That's right!', 'Read & enjoy.', 'Panta Rhei', 'Right to read.'), each with a '▶write' button and a thin timeline slider; top bar 'get license' and '▶write all'
instances.feel: Magic-slate: the computer writes your words like a hand would
instances.ux: Type in any sample; ▶write animates it being written stroke by stroke; drag the 'write frame' slider (0–1000) to scrub; '▶write all' plays every row at once; two writestyle modes per row
instances.learn: When the font has a time axis, the tester's main control is a play button and a timeline, not size or weight

reconstruction.layout: Full screen; top bar with two buttons; six rows each = a wide SVG stage (viewBox 0 -100 7000 1200, i.e. ~6:1) over a contenteditable line, then a stagemenu row (button + full-width range)
reconstruction.behaviour: contenteditable input mirrored into an SVG stage; play button animates the write frame 0→1000 (the font's time axis / stroke order); slider scrubs; writestyle attribute switches between two writing renderings
reconstruction.content: Short first-person reading affirmations for children
reconstruction.html: section.example > div.stageContainer[writestyle][fontstyle][weight] > svg.stageSVG + div.stageInput[contenteditable] ; div.stagemenu > button.write + input.writeFrame[type=range min=0 max=1000]

instances.look: White reading screen with a book-like article: big bold italic title 'Introducing Kermit / A Typeface for Kids', grey italic standfirst, '— Rob McKaughan (Microsoft)', then an indented single column of body text set in Kermit with italic titles (Harry Potter, Narnia)
instances.feel: Like a well-set children's book essay
instances.ux: Three essays ('Introducing Kermit' by Rob McKaughan, 'Time to play' by Underware, 'Hints of paradigm shifts' by Gerry Leonidas) picked from an essay index; superscript footnote links jump to numbered notes; lazy-loaded figures (prosody captioning, variable typography, HOI vs linear interpolation)
instances.learn: Invite outside voices (client, critic) to write the story and set it as a proper essay with footnotes: the read view doubles as a long text specimen

reconstruction.layout: Single column ~720px wide from x≈200 on white; title, standfirst, byline, then paragraphs with first-line indents (p.indent) and figure images at column width; footnotes list at the end of each article
reconstruction.typography: Title ~58px KermitItalic wght ~800, leading 1.1; standfirst ~30px KermitItalic grey #909090; byline ~16px Zeitung grey; body ~20px/1.6 KermitRoman with italics; footnote markers as sups
reconstruction.behaviour: Essay index (centre-left button) switches article #article1/2/3; footnote anchors; lazy images
reconstruction.content: Three real essays on readability for kids, dyslexia, prosody captioning and writable fonts
reconstruction.assets: Essay figures (specimen photo, prosody caption examples, interpolation diagrams, a GIF)
